critique: The screen has two legitimate anchors—the title/start block and the perspective note highway—but their nearly equal brightness creates a split first read instead of a controlled title → action → gameplay-preview sequence. The sunset disc and demo score add another high-contrast cluster above the highway. The hit line is unmistakable, yet the four key labels are crowded against the bottom edge and visually detached from their corresponding lanes, while the small mode and instruction text beneath the Start button is too faint to support the next step.
suggestion: Keep the title as the first read, make Start the clear second read, and slightly reduce the sunset/demo-score cluster so attention then moves naturally into the highway. Strengthen lane-to-key mapping by centering each key label within its lane immediately beneath the hit zone and providing enough bottom margin. Increase the legibility and grouping of the mode/control line under Start, and use the note placement to lead progressively toward the hit line rather than scattering equal-weight notes across the preview.
